newsitem.title: CANADA: Laidlaw soars to new heights on deals.
newsitem.headline: Laidlaw soars to new heights on deals.

text.p: Shares in Canadian waste and transportation firm Laidlaw Inc soared on Tuesday as investors cheered two major deals worth more than US$2 billion announced late on Monday.
Laidlaw's class B stock led actives on the Toronto Stock Exchange, jumping 1.20 to 17.40 in heavy mid-morning turnover of 4.7 million shares. The class B shares earlier hit a 52-week high of 17.60.
Laidlaw's class A stock improved 0.85 to 17.35 in turnover of 138,500 shares.

Laidlaw said after the market close on Monday that it planned to acquire Colorado-based American Medical Response Inc in a US$1.12 billion cash deal and merge it with its California-based MedTrans ambulance services unit.

In the other transaction, Laidlaw said it signed a letter of intent to sell its South Carolina-based Environmental Services unit for cash, shares and debt to Rollins Environmental Services of Wilmington, Delaware. Laidlaw would receive US$400 million in cash, 120 million Rollins common shares, and a US$350 million, 12-year, five percent convertible debenture.
"I think this is going to be very favourable for them," said Ira Katzin, an investment advisor with RBC Dominion Securities.

Katzin said the Rollins deal will further consolidate a fragmented industry and perhaps improve prices. The AMR acquisition allows Laidlaw to grow in a rapidly expanding heathcare transportation sector.
"We've got a (share price) target level of around C$19 and C$20 for the year and it will probably go higher when the dust settles," Katzin said.
